articles.title: 2 men seriously injured in overnight stabbings on King Street West
articles.summary: Two men were seriously injured during an overnight stabbings in Toronto’s Entertainment District, according to police. Emergency crews were called to the area of King Street West and Portland Street just after 4:30 a.m. on Friday for reports of a stabbing in the neighbourhood. articles.title: This couple says they are paying the price of Toronto's housing push
articles.summary: An elderly downtown couple says they’re shocked and upset that the city has approved a duplex next door to their three-story Victorian home that they say will tower metres above their chimney and render their fireplaces useless while blocking one window.

articles.title: Mamdani's populist style is all over the Toronto election race
articles.summary: Zohran Mamdani's 2025 mayoral campaign put a spotlight on cost of living issues and was characterized by colourful messaging, snappy social media videos and a where-there’s-a-will-there’s-a-way approach to making changes in New York — tactics many candidates in Toronto’s municipal election seem to be replicating.

articles.title: Mississauga’s top mayoral candidates facing off in 1st debate
articles.summary: Mississauga's leading mayoral candidates — incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish, former Mayor Bonnie Crombie, councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla — go face-to-face in the first debate of the municipal campaign. It will be carried live at 2:30 p.m. ET on all CBC platforms.

articles.title: Bonnie Crombie proposes extending TTC west into Mississauga if elected mayor
articles.summary: Mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie is pitching the idea of extending the TTC's Line 2 subway west from Kipling station to Sherway Gardens and into the centre of Mississauga.

articles.summary: Toronto police are searching for a man who allegedly sexually assaulted another person while riding their bicycle. articles.summary: A man was seriously injured after being struck by a vehicle in Mississauga. articles.title: Durham police chief denounces hate after 2 alleged hate-related offences
articles.summary: The chief of Durham Region's police service says he is concerned about an increase in hate-related incidents after two arrests this week in separate alleged offences.

articles.title: 3-day memorial run from Toronto to Ottawa kicks off to honour 7 fallen police officers
articles.summary: About 300 runners took off from Queen's Park this morning for a memorial run to Ottawa in honour of police officers who died in the line of duty this past year, including Toronto Const. Marc Pinizzotto, OPP Sgt. Brandon Malcolm and OPP Const. Tarun Bali.

articles.title: Peel police investigate suspected arson after 2 tow truck fires in Mississauga
articles.summary: Peel police are investigating a suspected arson after two tow trucks were found on fire in Mississauga Thursday morning.

articles.title: ‘We shouldn't have to beg,’ says chief of First Nation facing decades of mercury poisoning in Ontario
articles.summary: Grassy Narrows First Nation and Wabaseemoong Independent Nations continue to seek justice from the provincial and federal governments over decades of mercury poisoning caused by contamination that dates back to the 1960s and '70s. The First Nations' River Run Rally drew about 9,000 people to downtown Toronto on Wednesday. Here's what they want to see happen.
